statements.quote:
While powerful, current off-the-shelf models often struggle to adhere to established
stylistic principles or interpret precise design requirements. The resulting visual artifacts
can confuse designers rather than inspire (see Web Appendix A for an illustration).

We demonstrate
this relationship in Web Appendix B.4.

To gener-
ate the nuanced narratives, we employ an off-the-shelf image captioning model, JoyCaption,
which provides rich and holistic descriptions of visual arrangements and subtle stylistic nu-
ances embedded within the logo (fpgaminer, 2025).

statements.quote:
Full details of these studies are provided in
Web Appendix B.3.

All participants can view the creative brief that
includes information about the healthcare brand and a textual description of client pref-
erences (Appendix A provides an example).

The focal brand obtained the initial logos in a private crowdsourcing design contest in 2019. These
logos are not public to web search, thus designers in our study have no external access to logo exemplars
unless provided by us. The focal brand was also not included in the training of the generative pipeline in
Section 3.

Access to
the galleries is restricted to assigned designers based on their designer IDs.

In
Appendix B we provide the variable definitions and descriptive statistics.

To collect these ratings, we measured click attractiveness using an online survey, similar to Section 3.2.2
and Web Appendix B.3.

Our findings are consistent
across the two metrics; we report the embedding-based results in the main text and the
perception-based results in Appendix C.

In Web
Appendix C, we replicate the analysis using different definitions of the high-quality set and
demonstrate that our main findings are robust.

We provide the full results in Web Ap-
pendix C.

We further investigate whether AI intermediation improves the quality of top designs
using quantile regression (details in Web Appendix C).

In Appendix E we show that
specific core design elements – such as the medical cross, shield motif, and blue-green color
palette – are highly predictive of quality in this context.

Additionally, we show that this same pattern holds for the aggregate alignment measures documented
in Web Appendix B.3.

To
test this, we recruited professional designers to create “refined variations”—versions of the
AI outputs polished to a ready-to-use state with minimal conceptual modification (see Ap-
pendix D for details).

Randomization checks, presented in Web Appendix D, confirm there are no significant
differences in demographics or participation across conditions.

Detailed results and robustness checks using alternative definitions of high-quality
submissions are provided in Web Appendix D.2.

statements.quote:
In this section we provide additional robustness checks for our results in Section 4. We
provide the full table of experimental results using the main measures discussed in the text:
quality (Table WA-C.1) and originality (Table WA-C.2). For quality, we show in Table WA-
C.1 that our results are robust for the mean quality and selected quantiles in Figure 8 (Top
5%, 10%, 25%, and 50%). For embedding-based originality, we show in Table WA-C.2 that
our results are robust to the definition of ‘high quality’ by considering not only the top 50
in each condition, but also the top 100 in each condition as well as the top 200 or 400 in
all submissions. Tables WA-C.3 and WA-C.4 present the contrasts of condition estimates of
quality and embedding-based originality, respectively.

deposits.notes: Ancillary third-party repository, not a deposit of this paper's data or analysis code. The paper cites fpgaminer (2025), JoyCaption (GitHub repository), at PDF p. 34 and describes it as an off-the-shelf captioner at PDF p. 11. The citation supplies no URL; the named owner's repository was resolved and verified at this URL. The public page and the required recursive GitHub tree API both returned HTTP 200. The API tree was not truncated and contained 15 files at commit 8445b2e55db7856d522e44ae84e7415fcf3413f6. README.md and LICENSE were fetched in memory at that commit (both HTTP 200). They describe the general image-captioning model and its own pretraining data; neither mentions Xuekang Wu, AI Intermediation, Armor Health, Juneberry, or Timoshenko. The listed files are model code, documentation, example assets, and a training notebook; no focal-study participant records, arm labels, outcomes, or participant-linked designs were identified. The three false flags refer to S1/S2 research data, not to generic example prompts in the model repository. This dependency is recorded for completeness and does not establish availability of the authors' custom fine-tuning pipeline, replication code, or experimental data.

Unconfirmed author/title lead, not a verified dataset for this paper. DataCite searches for the first author returned DOI 10.21985/n2-dfgk-q722, Essays on Generative Models for Creative Design in Marketing, by Wu, Xuekang (2026), with resource type Dissertation. The metadata endpoint https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.21985/n2-dfgk-q722 returned HTTP 200; contentUrl, descriptions, sizes, formats, relatedIdentifiers, and rightsList provide no file or licensing evidence. The recorded landing page returned HTTP 403 with a generic Forbidden response. Stopped there; no login, access request, or circumvention was attempted. Could not establish whether this dissertation contains either experiment, enumerate its files, or inspect any data. The empty files list means unknown, not zero files; a 403 response alone does not establish an account requirement, embargo, or request-only data policy.

notes:
Scope: the complete March 2, 2026 working paper was read from its markdown conversion, including References, main-document Appendices A-E, and the appended Web Appendix (69 PDF pages). Relevant statement locators and verbatim quotations were checked with PyMuPDF; quotations preserve PDF line breaks and line-end hyphenation. No explicit data/code availability statement, preregistration statement, data-on-request promise, embargo, or link to a study-data/replication repository was found. The statements record the relevant materials access, cited code dependency, and appendix pointers; they are not promises of a data release. The PDF has no external URI link annotations or embedded file attachments. Both form.data_and_code URLs are empty.

The overall status none_found means no confirmed study-specific data or replication-code deposit was found for S1 or S2. The two deposit entries retain an explicitly cited third-party model repository and an unconfirmed first-author dissertation lead for auditability. General JoyCaption source code does not warrant classifying the paper's own data/code as public. The private-exemplar and assigned-gallery restrictions describe experimental information access; they do not establish that research data are currently available on request or under restricted access.

Public manuscript/materials check: https://artemtimoshenko.com/ returned HTTP 200 and the focal research entry linked only the manuscript, with no associated data, code, or supplementary-data link. https://artemtimoshenko.com/assets/papers/AI%20Intermediation%20March%202026.pdf returned HTTP 200 (4,332,926 bytes); its SHA-256 was a4c02a987d58b337fed54d8f530238fc031c1b4d69172a523fafc77c767a0417, identical to the local PDF. Brief examples, design illustrations, method descriptions, and aggregate tables are already in that manuscript. They are not a standalone participant-data deposit.

Publisher/SSRN check: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5371575 redirected to https://www.ssrn.com/abstract=5371575 and returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge. Stopped without passing the challenge, so SSRN supplementary-file availability remains unknown. Other literal domains mentioned in the paper were checked: https://www.freelancer.com/ returned HTTP 200 (general recruitment/design platform, no focal gallery URL is given), and https://stability.ai/ returned HTTP 200 (general company site, named only in the CLIP model's computing-cluster credit). Neither is evidence of a study-data deposit.

Search scope: full-title, shorter-title, and first-author searches were performed through the four specified APIs with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no identifying credentials. Each distinct request and its observed result count/status is recorded in searches. Zenodo's initial size=100 requests returned HTTP 400; the same queries succeeded using the permitted public size=25. OSF queries use the requested filter[title] endpoint, so author-name searches there only search node titles, not every contributor's projects. Broader Xuekang searches reduce dependence on creator-name order. Only metadata-mismatched results were excluded without downloading them. No relevant OSF, Harvard Dataverse, or Zenodo node/record was identified, so no study repository file-list endpoint was available to inspect.

No participant or output data table was found to read. We cannot derive the missing per-person outcome means/SDs/SEs, distinct-designer counts in quality-selected originality subsets, perception-originality output/designer counts, or fluency SDs/tests from any identified public data file. Nor could we recover the omitted S1 Variation(4) analysis coefficient/specification, settle Appendix E arm composition, or resolve the replication quality inference discrepancy. The task is visual logo design: diversity would require participant-linked submitted images or suitable embeddings/features with arm labels, and none were located. No new statistics were calculated.

Confidence is medium: the full saved paper and its current author-hosted copy were checked, and all four prescribed repository searches ultimately responded, but SSRN and the potentially related dissertation landing page were inaccessible. Absence of a located deposit is not proof that no public deposit exists.
